must_remember: The mean free path $\lambda$ is given by the Maxwell corrected formula $\lambda = \frac{1}{\sqrt{2} \pi n d^2}$.
At constant pressure, mean free path is directly proportional to absolute temperature $T$.
At constant temperature, mean free path is inversely proportional to pressure $P$ and number density $n$.
Collision frequency $f$ is defined as the average number of collisions per unit time and equals $\frac{\bar{v}}{\lambda}$.
The coefficient of viscosity $\eta$ and thermal conductivity $K$ of a gas are independent of pressure over moderate ranges.

glossary.meaning: The statistical average distance a gas molecule travels between successive collisions.
The average number of collisions experienced by a single gas molecule per unit time.
The number of molecules present per unit volume of the gas.
The effective diameter of a gas molecule treated as a hard sphere for collision cross-section.

comparisons.title: Dependence of Mean Free Path
rows: Higher pressure means higher number density and closer molecules.
Larger cross-sectional area increases collision probability.
